design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that patients were prospectively assigned to three groups using block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Block randomization was reported, but the method used to generate the sequence and allocation concealment were not described, and there was a statistically significant baseline imbalance in obesity prevalence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prospective randomization of the patients was carried out using block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: The visibly different intraoperative procedures precluded blinding of surgical personnel, while masking, protocol deviations, intervention adherence, and use of an intention-to-treat analysis were not explicitly reported, although all randomized patients appear to have been analyzed in their assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The Genta-Coll® resorb sponge (5 × 20 cm) was inserted between and under the sternal halves during sternum osteosynthesis at the end of the operation.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 996 randomized patients are included in the reported group denominators, but completeness and methods of three-month outcome ascertainment are not explicitly documented and deaths could preclude infection assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 996 patients investigated, 332 patients (33.3%) were prospectively randomized into the S-group, whereas 336 patients (33.7%) were randomized into the G-group and 328 patients (32.9%) into the I-group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sternal SSI is an appropriate clinical outcome and was evaluated over the same period in all groups, but assessor blinding and standardized adjudication or diagnostic criteria for classifying superficial versus deep SSI were not clearly reported, allowing possible detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The incidence of superficial and deep sternal wound infections was evaluated during hospital stay and after 3 months postoperatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary endpoints and a power calculation are described, but no protocol, trial registration, or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported to exclude selective choice among outcome definitions, time points, or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary study end-point was to analyse the incidence of superficial and deep sternal SSI... The secondary study end-point was to determine independent risk factors for an increased SSI rate of the sternum.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The trial reports block randomization and complete group denominators, but lacks details on allocation concealment, blinding, intervention deviations, follow-up completeness, blinded outcome adjudication, and prespecification; the baseline obesity imbalance adds concern about the randomization process.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated using a computer-generated random sequence, stratified by center, with variable block sizes and sealed-envelope concealment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence generation and envelope concealment were appropriate, but post-randomization exclusions and notable baseline imbalances in steroid and aspirin use leave some concern about the analyzed groups despite otherwise similar characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with a variable block size of 8, 12, or 16 patients and was stratified for center. Assignments were concealed in sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and postoperative assessors were blinded and analysis was described as intention-to-treat, but operating staff necessarily knew allocation after envelope opening and the reported analysis excluded randomized patients who withdrew or were excluded after allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All analyses were made on an intention-to-treat basis, ie, patients who died and those reoperated on for bleeding or other reasons during the follow-up period were included in the analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome ascertainment was available for 1,950 of 1,956 participants entering the study, so missing outcome data were minimal and unlikely to materially bias the effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thus, 1956 patients entered the study. Six of these could not be reached at the follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sternal wound infection was assessed using prespecified CDC-based criteria by blinded postoperative personnel, with final classifications completed before the randomization code was broken.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All classifications were made by the same person, a senior surgeon (Ö.F.), before the randomization code was broken.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary endpoint and statistical methods were prespecified in the report, but no trial registration or analysis protocol is reported and numerous subclassifications and subgroup analyses allowed potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subgroup analyses with regard to bacterial etiology, depth of infection and established preoperative risk groups (diabetes and high body mass index [BMI]) were conducted.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Randomization and blinded outcome measurement were strong and outcome missingness was minimal, but post-randomization exclusions/withdrawals, possible deviations from a strict intention-to-treat approach, baseline imbalances, and absence of a reported prespecified protocol or registration prevent a low-risk judgment.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that patients were randomized to gentamicin implant or control using sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although sealed-envelope allocation and broadly balanced baseline characteristics were reported, the method used to generate the sequence and whether envelopes were opaque, sequentially numbered, and inaccessible before enrollment were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomized to the gentamicin group or the control group using sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgeons and participants could not have been fully blinded to implant placement, and the paper does not explicitly report intervention fidelity, protocol deviations, or an intention-to-treat analysis, although all randomized analyzed patients appear to have remained in their assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients in the gentamicin group received a 10 cm!10 cm gentamicin-collagen implant... underneath their sternum before wound closure... The controls’ sternums were closed in a routine manner with steel wires, without a gentamicin implant.

domain_judgments.rationale: Infection outcomes were reported for all 542 analyzed patients over three months, with no outcome attrition indicated and only four deaths reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were followed-up three months after discharge from hospital.

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgical-site infection was measured in both groups using established CDC criteria, and final diagnoses were made by clinicians who were uninvolved in the study and blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The diagnosis of sternum infection was made either by a cardiac surgeon or an infection consultant who was not involved in this study and who did not know which study group each patient belonged to.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol, preregistration, or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, so selective choice among infection outcomes or analyses cannot be excluded despite straightforward reporting of the main outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Univariate analysis was performed using χ2 tests for categoric variables and t-tests for continuous variables. Values of P < 0.05 were considered to be significant.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment, lack of explicit information about deviations and intention-to-treat analysis, and absence of a protocol or preregistration. Outcome completeness and blinded, standardized infection assessment were reassuring.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that patients were prospectively randomized to gentamicin-collagen or identical placebo sponges, with randomization conducted by the Centre for Clinical Studies of Würzburg University Hospital.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization and centralized labeling were reported, but the sequence-generation method and allocation-concealment mechanism were not described, and several baseline imbalances raise some concern, although they could be due to chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization and blinding were carried out by the Centre for Clinical Studies of Würzburg University Hospital. After randomization, the 400 gentamicin-collagen sponges and the 400 placebo sponges were labeled with a sticker showing the randomization number.

domain_judgments.rationale: Identical placebo sponges and blinding make intervention-related deviations unlikely, but 20 patients were excluded for non-use of the specified sponge and the analysis was not clearly intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Some 80 of 800 patients (10%) could not be evaluated, the reasons being revision surgery because of bleeding (40x), perioperative mortality not associated with a wound infection (20x), and non-use of the specified sponge (20x).

domain_judgments.rationale: Ten percent of randomized/enrolled patients were excluded from analysis for post-randomization reasons, including bleeding revision, death, and non-use of the assigned sponge; group-specific missingness was not reported, and these events could be related to intervention and infection outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 720 of 800 (90%) of the screened patients were included in the study analysis after the end of the 30-day follow-up period after index surgery. Some 80 of 800 patients (10%) could not be evaluated.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sternal infections were assessed on the same schedule in both groups using prespecified CDC-based clinical and microbiological criteria, and identical sponges maintained blinding of surgeons and patients during outcome assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were examined once daily up to the time of discharge for wound healing and signs of infection... DSWI and SSWI were defined on the basis of the criteria of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and primary and secondary outcomes were identified, but the registration identifier appears incomplete and no protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan is available here to exclude selective choice among multiple analyses, including adjusted, survival, and subgroup analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered at Current Controlled Trials Limited, London with the assign ISRCTN 20849.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because 10% of participants were excluded after randomization for potentially outcome-related reasons without reporting missingness by group, making bias from missing outcome data plausible. Additional concerns arise from incomplete reporting of sequence generation/concealment, lack of clear intention-to-treat analysis, and limited information for assessing selective reporting.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports prospective random allocation after surgical incision using a central interactive voice-response system with site stratification and random block sizes.

domain_judgments.rationale: A central system generated concealed allocation using stratification and random block sizes, and reported baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization occurred after surgical incision using a central randomization interactive voice response system, thus providing complete allocation concealment. The randomization scheme was stratified by site and random block sizes were used.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although surgeons were unblinded, care was protocolized, adherence to assigned treatment was very high, deviations were minor, and the primary analysis appropriately followed intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 753 patients randomized to receive 2 gentamicin-collagen sponges, 741 received 2 sponges (98.5%), 1 received 1 sponge (0.1%), and 10 did not receive any sponges (1.3%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome information was available for 1490 of 1502 participants, with only 0.8% lacking primary-endpoint information and similarly low, balanced loss to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Only 12 of 1502 individuals did not contribute information to the primary end point. Due to the small effect made by these 12 patients (0.8%), in the final primary analysis with the intentto-treat population we treated them as not having sternal wound infection.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was defined using standardized criteria and centrally adjudicated by an independent committee blinded to treatment assignment, limiting differential measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The independent clinical events classification committee was composed of 3 infectious disease experts blinded to the treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the primary outcome and analysis population were clearly prespecified, and the reported primary analysis follows that plan, with no indication of selective choice among eligible primary analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary statistical analysis was performed using standard intentionto-treat methods. Unless otherwise indicated, all results in the text, tables, and figures reflect the intent-to-treat population.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is low. Randomization and concealment were robust, primary outcome ascertainment was blinded and standardized, missing data and intervention deviations were minimal, and the prespecified intention-to-treat analysis was reported.
